featured_reviews.name: Karthik Iyer
featured_reviews.review_text:
"I traveled from very far specifically to visit Rekdee - Taste of the Streets in Mulund for their late night food. The experience was a masterclass in how inconsistent management and staff can drive away genuine customers.

The Logical Contradiction:
Upon arrival, the boy at the counter informed me that Misal Pav was not available, but Tari Pav was. When I questioned the logic—given that both dishes share the exact same Tari (curry) and Pav—he failed to provide a valid reason. He then claimed a specific '12 AM to 4 AM' rule where Misal Pav is simply not served. I initially accepted this as a business policy maybe thinking that tarri pav has more profit and it consumes less tari as compared to a misal so they can make around 4-5 tari pavs instead of making 1 misal for profit, choosing to be reasonable and patient.

The Blatant Bias:
The situation changed 10 minutes later when a different family arrived. It was clear the management was partial to this specific group. Suddenly, the '12 AM to 4 AM' rule vanished, and the same staff member announced he was taking 'last orders' for Misal Pav for them. When confronted, he shamelessly claimed the Misal had 'magically' come back into stock. Only after being caught in this lie did he dismissively say, 'If you want now, we can give you,' which entirely missed the point of my concern regarding fair treatment.

The Linguistic Insult & Cowardice:
When I advised the staff that rules should be consistent for everyone, the boy cowardly hid behind the owner, claiming he was just following orders—despite being the one who originally gave me the 'lecture.' To make matters worse, both the owner and the boy began speaking in Gujarati, assuming I wouldn't understand their comments about a 'mess being created.' They were visibly stunned when I informed them that I understood every word of their mockery.

The ‘Go Ahead and Write’ Dare:
When I told the staff that such an unprofessional experience deserved a public review, the boy arrogantly responded with, 'Yeah, go ahead and write.'
To the Owner: Here is the review your staff requested. It is disappointing to see an owner stand by while staff lies to customers and then joins them in mocking a guest in a different language. Petrol and time were wasted on a recommendation that clearly doesn't value its patrons

featured_reviews.name: vru
featured_reviews.review_text:
Two areas of improvement would be allowing customers to choose two different mocktails under the offer, especially since all mocktails are priced the same.

Another thing to improve is the coordination between staff members—there was a noticeable communication gap while placing our order.

Visited The Food Studio near Nahur Railway Station and had a generally pleasant experience. We were seated within 5 minutes, and the ambiance was nice with a large TV setup in the center, adding a lively vibe to the place.

We started with French fries and a few starters: Jhinga Koliwada, Makhmali Kumbh, Pomfret Tandoori, and Chicken Burnt Garlic. The Jhinga Koliwada was the highlight—crispy and flavorful. Makhmali Kumbh is a great vegetarian option, stuffed with cheese and tasted quite good. However, the Pomfret Tandoori didn’t meet expectations—the masala lacked punch.

For the main course, we ordered Sabzi Peshawari with roti. It leaned towards the sweeter side, possibly due to the mix of paneer, mushrooms, and green peas. Not bad if you enjoy mildly sweet gravies.

We also tried the mocktail Mulokai under their Buy 1 Get 1 Free offer. The taste was average.

Overall, a good experience with room for a few improvements.

featured_reviews.name: Vijay Dhonde
featured_reviews.review_text:
TFT Mulund: Beautiful Ambience, Average Food, Poor Hospitality

Last night, we visited Mulund’s The Food Town (TFT) to celebrate wife’s birthday and make it a truly memorable occasion.

On the culinary side, the Mushroom Soup was delicious and well-prepared, while the Mexican Sizzler, though served average hot, was only average in taste. The Avocado Sushi too felt quite ordinary, lacking the flavor one would expect. When we ordered the Sizzler Brownie with Ice Cream, we were informed that the ice cream was melting, compelling us to cancel. Overall, the food quality and presentation were below expectations.

However, what left us most disappointed was the lack of warmth and sensitivity in hospitality. Despite TFT having three beautifully decorated side tables, which could have made our special day more memorable with photographs, our request to be relocated was denied. The waiter directed us to Mr. Vivek Asthana, who, instead of showing flexibility or customer empathy, flatly refused stating that the tables were reserved for larger groups—even though one such table remained vacant throughout our visit (as seen in the attached photograph). Ironically, another table with only three guests was being used, raising questions about consistency in policy.

When I suggested that hospitality should prioritize enhancing the experience of guests already present rather than waiting for potential walk-ins, Mr. Asthana maintained his refusal. This rigid approach not only dampened the spirit of our celebration but also raised concerns about the basic principles of guest satisfaction and service etiquette.

Towards the end, a group of teenagers entered, creating a noisy, chaotic, fish-market-like atmosphere that ruined the dining vibe. After informing,  though Mr. Asthana later shifted them, the overall experience was already compromised.

Frankly, I am unable to understand why Mr. Vivek Asthana chose to keep a table vacant rather than allow a genuine guest to create memories on a special occasion.

Is this truly what modern hospitality management teaches—denial over delight, rigidity over responsiveness, and policy over people?

To make things worse, no solution or replacement was offered. ₹847 completely wasted along with my craving for good Chinese food.

Very disappointing experience. Definitely not ordering from or visiting Food Town, Mulund again.

Jai Jalaram's Tasty Ice Bhel in Mulund West and I must say, it exceeded my expectations. At Rs. 40, this street food snack is an absolute steal!

The ice bhel was a refreshing twist on the classic bhel puri, with a unique combination of sweet and savory flavors. The coolness of the cool icy chatni complemented the spicy and tangy flavors of the bhel perfectly, making for a delicious and satisfying snack.

The portion size was average, and the ingredients were fresh and flavorful. I especially loved the crunch of the sev and the juicy bursts of flavor from the pomegranate seeds.

The staff was friendly and attentive, and the stall was clean and well-maintained. Overall, Jai Jalaram's Tasty Ice Bhel is a must-try for anyone looking for a tasty and affordable street food snack in Mulund West. I highly recommend it!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Jhulelal is a chaat corner which ūdoles out some mean desserts as well.

This place is owned & managed by a Sindhi gentleman, Sindhi's are known for their chaat items.

GULAB JAMUN [INR 20 per piece]
They serve an amazing & out of the world Gulab Jamun. Oblong in shape, soft within & syrup properly absorbed by each & every piece. Each Jamun is stuffed with a piece of Pistachio & honestly eating just 2 is not enough for the soul.
RECOMMENDED

PANI PURI [INR 30]
They serve Puri stuffed with boondi soaked in water & then dipped in a sweet chutney & spicy water. As usual, one can customise the taste as per preference. The taste of the spicy water differs from the usual found commonly but it's nice.

DAHI MIRCHI [INR 40]
They dip a big Bhavnagari mirchi in bean batter & deep dry it. The fried mirchi is cut into roundels & then topped with sweet & spicy chutney, thick creamy & sweet Dahi. It is then served with their in-house chaat masala which gives that extra flavour to the dish.
RECOMMENDED

Their specialty is DAHI WADA [INR 40] which is very very nice & often gets over a bit too soon.

SEV PURI [INR 35] & RAGDA PATTICE is also nice. Actually the secret of their flavour lies in the chutney, sweet & spicy.

Price wise it's very pocket friendly. Hygiene factor is well taken care of & service isn't anything to complain.

Jai Jhulelal warrants multiple visits because the Gulab Jamun is too good.

I recently visited Mukesh Pav Bhaji in Mulund West Khau Galli, which is a popular street food spot and seems quite well known among locals. The stall was busy when we visited, which usually indicates that people like the food here.

Some people may actually prefer this style because it feels less heavy and possibly uses fewer artificial flavor enhancers.
Overall, it is a good place to try once if you are exploring the street food in Mulund West Khau Galli. The masala pav is worth tasting.
Also, if you are already in the area, you can try pani puri at Gupta Panipuri Centre, which is located nearby in the pani puri galli. Their pani puri is quite popular among locals.

featured_reviews.name: Ashish Balachandran
featured_reviews.review_text:
❌ Urban Tadka – Mulund West: Inconsistent Food, Disappointing Execution

Visited Urban Tadka in Mulund West expecting a rich North Indian dining experience, but sadly, the evening was filled with more misses than hits. The vibe and branding promise a lot—but the food didn’t live up to it.

⸻

🍗 Happy Chicken Tikka – Underdone & Flat

The chicken was quite raw inside, with spices that felt slapped on rather than blended in. Texture was off and flavor didn’t settle. Disappointing, especially for something that’s supposed to be a highlight.

⸻

🐟 Fish Tikka – The Only Redeemer

This was the best dish of the evening. Perfectly cooked, well spiced, flaky and hot. If only the rest of the meal had matched this level.

⸻

🌶️ Garlic Chutney – Always Great

Still one of their strengths—bold, spicy, and garlicky. Goes well with almost anything.

⸻

🫓 Masala Papad – Shockingly Bad

I’ve had good masala papad here in the past, but this time it was very poorly done—soggy in parts, unevenly topped, and clearly rushed. It was a huge letdown, especially for such a simple dish.

⸻

🍷 Sangria – Just Syrupy Sweetness

This wasn’t sangria—it tasted like fruit syrup mixed with soda. No wine flavour, no balance, and way too sweet. It felt like a mocktail trying to pass as something it’s not.

⸻

🍮 Jalebi & Rabadi – Uneven Again
•	Rabadi: Thick, creamy, and well-made. A small win at the end of the meal.
•	Jalebi: Absolutely terrible. Not only was it soggy and bland, but it had a strong chemical smell—almost like bleach, which was shocking and off-putting.

⸻

💬 Final Thoughts

Urban Tadka Mulund is clearly struggling with quality control. From raw chicken and bad jalebi to sloppy basics like masala papad, this meal felt rushed and careless. The fish tikka, garlic chutney, and rabadi were the only saving graces.

⸻

❌ Final Verdict

Not worth the hype or the price. When half the items are badly executed—and one smells like cleaning fluid—it’s a red flag.
Urban Tadka needs to seriously rework their kitchen consistency if they want to live up to their name.

Would not return in a hurry.
🍗👎🍮🥴

featured_reviews.name: Tushar Sinagare
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mumbai's food scene is constantly evolving, but every now and then a restaurant arrives that creates a genuine buzz among food lovers. One such place is --> 'Delhi Se', Mulund, the viral restaurant chain that has quickly become one of the city's most talked-about dining destinations.

Known for serving authentic vegetarian North Indian street food, Delhi Se has built a cult following... bringing ingredients, spices, and even specialized chefs directly from Delhi to recreate the bold, punchy flavors of Chandni Chowk.

A Smoky Start – Tandoori Soya Chaap 😊
We began our culinary journey with the Tandoori Soya Chaap. Prepared using premium-quality soya sticks, the chaap was marinated in a thick blend of hung curd and robust Delhi-style spices before being cooked to perfection. This resulted in a  beautifully charred and smoky exterior that gives way to a super-soft, melt-in-the-mouth center. Every bite was packed with flavor and set the tone for what was to come.

Next came was the King of Chaats – Raj Kachori. This grand, king-sized crispy shell was generously stuffed with boiled potatoes and chickpeas. It was then drenched in creamy sweet dahi, tangy tamarind chutney, spicy mint chutney, and topped with a generous layer of sev. The combination of crunch, sweetness, tanginess, and spice created a perfect explosion of flavors and textures. It was every bit as indulgent as a great Delhi-style chaat should be.

But the Star Attraction none other than – Virat Kohli Wale Chole Bhature our main course. The bhaturas were huge, fluffy, perfectly stuffed, and remarkably non-greasy. They paired beautifully with the rich and perfectly spiced dark Pindi Chole, accompanied by pickle and mint chutney.
It is easy to understand why this dish has become synonymous with Delhi Se. Every element was executed flawlessly, delivering comfort, flavor, and satisfaction in equal measure.

Ending on a High our final dish – Chole Kulche - the same delicious Pindi Chole was served alongside incredibly soft and fluffy kulchas. These yeast-leavened flatbreads were lightly toasted on a tawa with a generous dollop of butter and finished with fresh coriander leaves. Simple yet incredibly satisfying, it was the perfect way to conclude our meal.

Hospitality That Wins Hearts - 🥰
While the food was exceptional, what truly elevated our experience was the hospitality.
The staff warmly recommended that we try their Rabri Jalebi. By then, we were completely full and politely mentioned that we would save it for our next visit. 😎
To our surprise, the staff graciously offered us a mini jalebi as a complimentary sampler.

This small gesture spoke volumes about the restaurant's customer-first approach. It reflected the passion and care that both the owners and staff have for ensuring guests leave with a smile.

Whether you're craving street-style chaat, indulgent Chole Bhature, or simply looking to experience a slice of Chandni Chowk in Mumbai, this place deserves a spot on your food bucket list. Would highly recommend Delhi Se to all food enthusiasts. Visit with friends, family, or fellow foodies, and don't be surprised if one visit turns into many more. And yes, next time we're definitely ordering the Rabri Jalebi 🙏🏻

🍽️ Food
•	Aloo Chaat with Chole – Disappointing. The flavours didn’t come together, and it lacked the tang and punch you expect from good chaat. Felt below average overall.
•	Green Mint Chutney – Fresh, zesty, and well-balanced. Definitely one of the stronger items on the table.
•	Chole Bhature – The dish was uneven. The bhature were very well done—crispy outside, soft inside, and enjoyable. But the chole fell flat—under-spiced and lacking the depth of flavour that makes this dish shine.

⸻

✅ Final Verdict

Delhi Se, Mulund West has friendly service and some decent items (like the chaas, bhature, and mint chutney), but the core flavours in key dishes like chole and chaat need serious improvement.

Worth a try if you’re nearby, but don’t expect authentic Delhi street food flavours just yet. 🌟
